correctness.rationale: Set B(n)=n s(n), s(n)=sigma(n)−n; B(p²)=p²(p+1). Any solution n divides p²(p+1), split e=v_p(n)∈{0,1,2}. For e=2 n=p²d, d|p+1, d>1 makes proper divisor p² contradict s(n)=(p+1)/d; hence n=p². For e=0 n=d|p+1 and p²|s(d), impossible as s(d)≤d(d−1)/2≤p(p+1)/2<p². For e=1 n=pd, d|p+1, gcd(p,d)=1 and sigma multiplicativity yield d(d+(p+1)s(d))=p(p+1). Put p+1=dk: d(1+k s(d))=pk, hence d|k, k=dh, and modulo h forces h=1; p+1=d², primality gives d=2,p=3,n=6. Both B(6)=B(9)=36. All primes covered, including p=2; independent exact divisor enumeration corroborates first 62 primes, not a proof of all primes.
